meta.title: Adapdev — bespoke software for Australian small business
meta.description: Adapdev is a Brisbane software partnership. We build full-fit custom software for sole traders, small businesses and small law firms — on hardware you own, in the language you already use. ADMS is available now; the Home Dialysis Tracker is in development for 2027.

changes.title: Four things we do differently from the browser-tab default

cards.title: Shaped around your workflow, not ours
cards.description: We start by learning how you already run the business, then shape the software to that. Clients, matters, jobs — whatever you call them, that's what the interface calls them too. No forced re-training.

cards.title: Speaks the language you already use
cards.description: A tradie has jobs. A solicitor has matters. A dialysis patient has sessions. We don't flatten those into a one-size-fits-all 'record' — the vocabulary is yours and the UI follows.

cards.title: Lives on your hardware
cards.description: On-premises is the default, cloud only when it genuinely helps. Your data sits on hardware you own, works when the internet doesn't, and never arrives on an invoice you didn't authorise.

cards.title: No subscription treadmill
cards.description: Products are sold as one-off licences; bespoke work is fixed-price per engagement. No per-seat multiplier, no 'the plan you need is the one above', no cloud bill in US dollars.

how.title: Four steps from first email to in production
how.body: We don't pitch and run. Every engagement — product or bespoke — follows the same shape, and you decide whether to keep going at every step.

steps.title: Scope
steps.description: You tell us what you do and where it hurts. We listen, ask the awkward questions, and come back with a written summary of what the work would involve. No charge.
steps.imageAlt: Light radiating from a single point

steps.title: Design
steps.description: A short written design — screens, data model, where the data lives — and a fixed quote. You sign it (or you don't). Either way the design is yours to keep.

steps.title: Build
steps.description: Short iterations, with you reviewing a working slice at each one. Nothing is a surprise at the end because nothing was hidden in the middle.

steps.title: Hand over
steps.description: We install, train, and leave you a written runbook. Support is one address, and the developer who shipped the code is the person who answers it.
steps.imageAlt: Two surfaces meeting at an edge

faq.title: The questions most people start with

card.title: Something more specific?
card.text: We reply the same working day.

items.q: How do you price a project?
items.a: Products are a one-off licence per installation, with twelve months of updates included; see /adms for ADMS pricing. Bespoke work is fixed-price per engagement, quoted from a short written design we produce together. No per-hour meter, no per-seat multiplier. If a change is in scope we don't invoice again; if it's not, we agree a change before we do the work.

A product install — ADMS, say — is usually under a day from signed quote to first filed document. A bespoke build runs from four to twelve weeks depending on scope; longer engagements get split into releases so you see working software monthly rather than all at once at the end.

items.q: Where are you based, and can you work outside Australia?
items.a: Brisbane, Queensland. Most of our work is Australian small business because that's who we understand best; we do not take overseas engagements at this point. Everything we ship runs locally, so time zones only matter for conversation, not for the product.

items.q: Can we run the software without you after launch?
items.a: Yes — that is the point of the model. Every product and every bespoke build ships with a written runbook, an on-site admin login, and the ability to export every byte of your own data. If you stop paying Adapdev, the software you already have keeps running.

.NET on the server side (ASP.NET Core, Entity Framework), WPF with the Prism framework for Windows desktop clients, and web front-ends in Astro or Vite/React when the brief calls for a browser. SQL Server and SQLite are our default databases. All choices we can live with for a decade of maintenance; none chosen to pad a resume.

items.q: Who do you NOT work with?
items.a: Businesses that want to buy headcount reductions as a feature, or that want software designed to make it harder for a customer to leave. If your idea of value is a lock-in the end user can't unwind, we're the wrong partnership.
